entities.name: Isolated ALP suggests bone source
observations: Normal GGT, bilirubin, aminotransferases, and other liver tests make a hepatic source of isolated alkaline phosphatase elevation less likely; repeat ALP with bone-specific ALP or isoenzymes is the ideal immediate localization step.
Total alkaline phosphatase with liver-function tests is a first-line biochemical screen for metabolically active Paget disease.

entities.name: Paget disease of bone
observations: In an asymptomatic older adult with persistent bone-derived ALP elevation, targeted plain radiographs of pertinent skeletal regions are preferred for diagnosis.
Radionuclide bone scintigraphy is used after radiographic confirmation to map the extent of metabolically active disease, including clinically silent lesions.

entities.name: Offered-choice limitation
observations: The ideal immediate test of repeat total ALP with bone-specific ALP or ALP isoenzymes is not among the answer choices; among the listed tests, bone scintigraphy is the test most aligned with evaluating occult multifocal Paget disease after biochemical suspicion, although targeted radiographs would ordinarily precede it.
